input.rationale: Add the second-boundary receipt to the startup account: at MaxAppendEntries=1024 the same 128-batch capacity stops 131073 committed entries while 131072 complete in 45 ms. The limitation that no non-default boundary had been exercised is replaced by the two measured boundaries, and the earlier cases remain as they were. This update also records the RecoverCluster contract read while surveying the remaining authority paths: the configuration comes from the operator and all retained commands are replayed before the log is deleted, so no defect is asserted for that path.

knowledge.statement: RecoverCluster refuses to run without existing state, restores the newest usable snapshot, then replays every log entry after the snapshot index, applying only LogCommand entries to the FSM and tracking the last index and term; it then writes a new snapshot carrying the caller-supplied configuration with configuration index 1 and deletes the entire log range. The recovered configuration is therefore the operator's parameter rather than anything derived from the log, and entries the node held without cluster-wide commitment become part of the recovered baseline.
knowledge.conditions: Operator-invoked catastrophic recovery with existing log, stable or snapshot state.

interpretations.rationale: Conclusion: violated. With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft does not complete a legal replay of already-committed log entries once the replay needs more than 128 FSM dispatch batches; the caller never receives the *Raft, so the node has no way to start, serve or shut down. This is a startup progress failure, not a decision-safety failure: no commit, vote or membership decision was observed to be wrong. Evidence. Receipt d61420dbc49a4072937b040aac55a51c (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): parsed index 1, seeded commit-tracking store with 8192 committed entries = exactly 128 batches at MaxAppendEntries=64, returned=true in 5 ms; parsed index 3, the retained state of a real single-node cluster that committed 8300 commands through the leader/commit/apply path and then snapshotted at index 8302 above the staged commit index, replay 0 batches, returned=true in 0 ms; parsed index 5, the same seeded store with 8193 entries = 129 batches, returned=false after 5000 ms with one newly blocked (*Raft).processLogs goroutine and one newly blocked (*Raft).restoreFromCommittedLogs goroutine; parsed index 7, the same real-cluster prefix without a snapshot, staged commit 8300 = 130 batches, returned=false after 5000 ms with the same two newly blocked goroutines. Successor receipt 87aea51bbd8a4b579f138f2c4986343a (completed, tests_passed, exit 0) reproduced all four outcomes (parsed indices 1, 3, 7, 9) and added parsed index 5: the identical 8193-entry store state that hangs at MaxAppendEntries=64, replayed as 9 batches with MaxAppendEntries=1024, returned=true in 2 ms. That comparison holds entry count, log content, staged commit index and snapshot state fixed and varies only the batch size, so the stall is attributable to the number of batches relative to the 128-slot channel rather than to log volume, snapshot handling, store state or the producing cluster; the goroutine match in both hanging cases localizes the block to processLogs invoked from restoreFromCommittedLogs. Mechanism from source: api.go:606 calls restoreFromCommittedLogs before any background goroutine exists; api.go:753 calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); raft.go:1303-1313 sends each commitTuple batch into fsmMutateCh and selects only on that send and on r.shutdownCh; fsmMutateCh has capacity 128 (api.go:560); its only reader runFSM (fsm.go:241) is started at api.go:637 after NewRaft returns; api.go:1065 is the only closer of shutdownCh and is reachable only through a *Raft. After 128 successful sends the 129th send therefore has no producer and no possible closer, so the block is permanent rather than slow. Consequence under the exercised conditions: a node restarting with the documented RestoreCommittedLogs option and with more than 128*MaxAppendEntries committed entries beyond its last snapshot hangs inside NewRaft indefinitely while reporting no error. The operational restart path was measured separately in receipt f032fc49841048c9877653db9f877b27: a three-voter cluster committed 8400 commands, one follower accumulated them and staged its own commit index at 8400 with last log index 8402, and only that follower was restarted. With a snapshot taken on that follower at 8400 the replay was 0 batches and NewRaft returned in 0 ms (parsed index 1, comparison holds); without the snapshot the same follower needed 132 batches and NewRaft had not returned after 5000 ms (parsed index 3, comparison violated). The boundary therefore reproduces from the follower's own appendEntries-driven commit staging, not only from a feeding leader. The boundary was then checked at a second batch size: receipt f8b98d790cc14664af8af17775d3cc48 replays 131072 committed entries at MaxAppendEntries=1024, which is exactly 128 batches, and NewRaft returned in 45 ms (parsed index 7, comparison holds), while 131073 entries, one entry further and therefore 129 batches, did not return within 5000 ms (parsed index 9, comparison violated). The same capacity limit therefore governs a replay whose entry count is sixteen times larger, so the boundary follows the batch count rather than the default entry count.

knowledge.assertion: NewRaft calls restoreFromCommittedLogs synchronously and processLogs flushes batches into fsmMutateCh while runFSM starts only after NewRaft returns.
The startup replay can enqueue at most 128 batches, so with DefaultConfig 8193 or more replayed entries beyond the last snapshot have no enabled progress path.

counterevidence: RestoreCommittedLogs is not part of DefaultConfig (config.go:329-341 leaves it false), and with the option disabled restoreFromCommittedLogs returns immediately (api.go:725-727), so default-configured nodes cannot reach the blocked path.

A snapshot at or near the commit index removes the replay entirely: parsed index 3 in both receipts restarted the same 8300-commit real prefix with replay_batches=0 and returned NewRaft immediately, so snapshot cadence bounds exposure to this path.

A larger MaxAppendEntries moves the boundary: parsed index 5 of receipt 87aea51bbd8a4b579f138f2c4986343a completed the very state that hangs at the default batch size, so a deployment that raises MaxAppendEntries enough for 128*MaxAppendEntries to cover its snapshot lag does not encounter the block.

The trigger observations are 5000 ms observation windows, not infinite runs; permanence is claimed from the source-level absence of any consumer before NewRaft returns and from shutdownCh having no closer outside Shutdown on the returned *Raft, not from the timeout alone.
No incorrect commit, applied entry, vote or membership decision was observed in any case; the evidence contradicts only startup progress.
limitations: The boundary is 128*MaxAppendEntries committed entries beyond the last snapshot, and it was exercised at two batch sizes: at 64 the boundary is 8192 entries (8193 blocked, 8192 returned) and at 1024 it is 131072 entries (131073 blocked, 131072 returned). The 128-slot fsmMutateCh capacity is not configurable and no case varied it.

The seeded cases supply the commit-tracking store state directly. Three restarts rest on a real prefix: a single-node leader (staged commit 8300, last log 8302, because the leader stages the pre-dispatch commit index) and a three-voter cluster follower in both the snapshot and no-snapshot cases (staged commit 8400, last log 8402).

The with-snapshot control eliminated the replay rather than shortening it, so real-prefix restarts whose replay is between 1 and 128 batches were not exercised; that recovery region is bracketed only by the seeded 9-batch case and inferred from source for the real prefix.

fsm_applied_sampled is one sample at the end of each window and was 0 in every case, including the returning controls where runFSM had not yet applied anything, so it is not used as evidence of completion.

Out of scope here: whether the installSnapshot and restoreUserSnapshot sends to the same channel can block indefinitely on a running node, where runFSM is already active and would provide backpressure rather than a permanent block.
interpretations.joint_history: Receipt 87aea51bbd8a4b579f138f2c4986343a is the successor of 1255b78953904846987cdc19826340c8-experiment under the same investigation: it retains the four case names, admissions and assertions unchanged, adds one case, and changes only the recorded max_append_entries field and the new case. The four retained result events agree with the earlier receipt (both controls returned, both triggers did not), so the two receipts describe the same subject at the same snapshot and their events can be read together; the question-level account therefore cites both rather than replacing the earlier witness. Receipt f032fc49841048c9877653db9f877b27 comes from a second experiment under this question rather than a revision of the first: it builds the committed prefix through a three-voter cluster and restarts a follower, where the earlier experiment restarted a single-node leader or a hand-seeded store. Its cases are named differently and its admissions are its own, so it is not a substitute for the earlier receipts; it is cited because it exercises the same RestoreCommittedLogs replay boundary on the operational restart shape with the same source-level mechanism. Receipt f8b98d790cc14664af8af17775d3cc48 is a further revision of the same experiment that adds the two MaxAppendEntries=1024 boundary cases; all earlier cases and assertions are unchanged, and its result at each of those cases matches the earlier receipts.

knowledge.statement: appendEntries raises the receiving term by first testing a.Term against r.getCurrentTerm() and later calling setCurrentTerm(a.Term), which writes the stable store and then the atomic term without comparing against the value it read, so the decision and the write are not a single atomic compare-and-set; the same function later deletes a conflicting log suffix from the first index whose term differs and appends the request's entries. Because the leader's heartbeat request carries only a header, a term and a leader address, its concurrent execution skips the previous-log check, stores no entries and never advances the commit index, so the term and leader updates are its only state effects.
knowledge.conditions: Any appendEntries invocation, including one delivered concurrently through the heartbeat fast-path; the heartbeat case has PrevLogEntry 0, no entries and LeaderCommitIndex 0.

knowledge.statement: NetworkTransport's connection handler decodes an AppendEntries request and treats it as a heartbeat exactly when the term is non-zero, a leader address is present, PrevLogEntry and PrevLogTerm are both zero, there are no entries and LeaderCommitIndex is zero; for that shape it looks up the registered heartbeat handler under its lock and, if set, calls it directly on the connection-handler goroutine and skips the consumer channel, otherwise it enqueues the request for the main thread.
knowledge.conditions: NetworkTransport with NewRaft having registered processHeartbeat; incoming AppendEntries request matching the heartbeat field pattern.

knowledge.statement: VerifyLeader sizes its quorum with quorumSize (voters/2+1, voters only) but registers the verify future with every entry of leaderState.replState, which startStopReplication creates for every configured server including non-voters; a successful heartbeat or AppendEntries response calls notifyAll(true), which increments the verify future's vote count and completes the verification once the count reaches the voter-sized quorum.
knowledge.conditions: Leader with at least one non-voter replication stream and fewer reachable voters than the voter quorum.

knowledge.statement: checkLeaderLease, unlike VerifyLeader, iterates the latest configuration and counts only servers whose Suffrage is Voter towards the contacted quorum, so the lease check and the verification path use different supporter sets.
knowledge.conditions: Leader loop lease check with a configuration containing non-voters.

knowledge.statement: appendConfigurationEntry dispatches the configuration entry with dispatchLogs and then, regardless of whether the entry was stored, sets the latest configuration to the new configuration at the index the entry would have occupied, reconfigures the commitment map and restarts replication; dispatchLogs answers the futures with the store error and moves the node to follower, leaving the in-memory latest configuration ahead of the stored log.
knowledge.conditions: Leader applying a configuration change whose StoreLogs call fails.

knowledge.statement: quorumSize, electSelf and setupLeaderState all derive their voter set and quorum from the node's latest configuration, so a latest configuration that is not present in the log governs elections and commitment for that node.
knowledge.conditions: Any node whose configurations.latest refers to an unstored configuration entry.

knowledge.statement: NetworkTransport's connection handler decodes an AppendEntries request and treats it as a heartbeat exactly when the term is non-zero, a leader address is present, PrevLogEntry and PrevLogTerm are both zero, there are no entries and LeaderCommitIndex is zero; for that shape it looks up the registered heartbeat handler under its lock and, if set, calls it directly on the connection-handler goroutine and skips the consumer channel, otherwise it enqueues the request for the main thread.
knowledge.conditions: NetworkTransport with NewRaft having registered processHeartbeat; incoming AppendEntries request matching the heartbeat field pattern.

knowledge.statement: VerifyLeader sizes its quorum with quorumSize (voters/2+1, voters only) but registers the verify future with every entry of leaderState.replState, which startStopReplication creates for every configured server including non-voters; a successful heartbeat or AppendEntries response calls notifyAll(true), which increments the verify future's vote count and completes the verification once the count reaches the voter-sized quorum.
knowledge.conditions: Leader with at least one non-voter replication stream and fewer reachable voters than the voter quorum.

knowledge.statement: checkLeaderLease, unlike VerifyLeader, iterates the latest configuration and counts only servers whose Suffrage is Voter towards the contacted quorum, so the lease check and the verification path use different supporter sets.
knowledge.conditions: Leader loop lease check with a configuration containing non-voters.

knowledge.statement: appendConfigurationEntry dispatches the configuration entry with dispatchLogs and then, regardless of whether the entry was stored, sets the latest configuration to the new configuration at the index the entry would have occupied, reconfigures the commitment map and restarts replication; dispatchLogs answers the futures with the store error and moves the node to follower, leaving the in-memory latest configuration ahead of the stored log.
knowledge.conditions: Leader applying a configuration change whose StoreLogs call fails.

knowledge.statement: quorumSize, electSelf and setupLeaderState all derive their voter set and quorum from the node's latest configuration, so a latest configuration that is not present in the log governs elections and commitment for that node.
knowledge.conditions: Any node whose configurations.latest refers to an unstored configuration entry.

knowledge.statement: RecoverCluster refuses to run without existing state, restores the newest usable snapshot, then replays every log entry after the snapshot index, applying only LogCommand entries to the FSM and tracking the last index and term; it then writes a new snapshot carrying the caller-supplied configuration with configuration index 1 and deletes the entire log range. The recovered configuration is therefore the operator's parameter rather than anything derived from the log, and entries the node held without cluster-wide commitment become part of the recovered baseline.
knowledge.conditions: Operator-invoked catastrophic recovery with existing log, stable or snapshot state.
